event: There is no threshold: beyond the stair's waymarker, trees simply begin.
The compass still swings five degrees; Wren walks south by the angle of the light.
The transition woodland is a real forest: shaggy oaks, tall ash, and trees she does not know.
Ghost elms: silver-green bark, smooth as polished stone, ghostly white in shade.
She touches one; the cool bark hums below hearing, up through her wrist.
Six inches higher the hum changes: the tree is a chord, not a single note.
A discovery identifies the ghost elm and its acoustic bark: +40 XP, Identification activates.

changes.note: Discovery: ghost elm identified, acoustic bark

event: She sketches the trunk and writes: ask the Rimfolk if they know why the bark hums.
The forest thickens southward: waist-high ferns, two-toned shrubs, spiraling vines.
The air grows warmer and thick with scent; the unnamed sweetness is stronger down here.
The three-note bird calls closer; something small rustles in the ferns and goes still.
Her road-warden's boots sink into the spongy leaf layer of a floor no one maintains.
[Wayfinder's Eye] hums: moss stories, scored heartwood, and tiny white flowers.
The cream flowers grow only where a ghost-elm root meets an oak root.
A discovery logs the unregistered boundary bloom: +45 XP; Environmental Reading activates.

changes.note: Discovery: boundary bloom at ghost-elm and oak root contact

event: She notes that the System tells what a thing is apart from how it relates.
She needs water, food, and a camp before the light fails under the canopy.
She hears chopping, and a young man's voice talking without pause about roots.
A lower voice says, 'Someone on the track. Stay.' Wren walks in openly.
She steps through ferns into a clearing: three lean-tos, a fire pit, drying racks.
A compact, forest-worn man in his fifties holds a gathering knife and weighs her.
Beside him a restless young man holds a dug root, dirty to the wrists.
The young man says nobody uses the Warden's Stair; the older man silences him: 'Hadley.'
'Theron Blackroot. Rimfolk. This is my camp.' Hadley Wynn gathers for him, and talks.
Wren gives her name; Theron says he knows who she is.
Neither speaks; Hadley breaks after twelve seconds: 'You're the Wayfinder.'
Theron asks how she managed the fourth switchback. 'Carefully,' she says.
He sits her on a flat stone and tells her that her left strap is torquing her spine.
He brings her cold limestone water that tastes like Millhaven's wells.
'I'm going to tell you to go back. And you're not going to go.' 'No.'
Theron says nothing written about the Thornwild stays accurate more than a season.
He knows Callum; three generations of his family have gathered the first five miles.
He tells of Deel, a Level 23 Ranger, who went twelve miles in and lost two days.
Below five miles is the deep forest the Rimfolk call the Crying Forest; it weeps.
He tells her, sixteen and without combat skills, to go back.
Wren says she hears him, and will learn the first five miles first.
'I'm planning to pay attention. And to ask you things, if you'll let me.'
Theron tells Hadley to show her the spring and the sound ground east of the ridge.
'You'll eat with us tonight. I have questions.'
Hadley leads her east along the ridge, talking about water, seeps and his father.
Hadley, a Level 7 Gatherer, asks what being a Wayfinder actually does.
At the seep she says the System gives her noticing a weight, and she carries places.
She tells him of the Warden's Shelf, like a second heartbeat in her chest.
Hadley, silent five whole seconds: 'That's not a tool. That's a relationship.'
He asks to show her a root he has been trying to understand.
At a sapling he shows ghost-elm laterals spiraling clockwise, straightening below 18 inches.
Wren links the spiral to the bark's resonance: the roots are drilling for something.
[Wayfinder's Eye] shows the soil darker and finer where the spiral roots have turned.
Hadley thinks the root grinds the soil; Wren says, 'Or feeds it.'
A multi-factor discovery on root and soil: +55 XP, Environmental Reading rises.

changes.note: Discovery: spiral roots alter the soil, multi-factor

event: She tells Hadley the System gives her hypotheses; it thinks out loud. He grins wide.
They return to camp as the green light cools toward twilight.
She pitches her tarp east of the ridge; Hadley brings ferns, naming each armful.
Theron builds the fire; ghost-elm won't burn, Hadley says, its hum puts the flame out.
Wren asks what heat without flame would do to the resonance; no one has ever tried.
Theron cooks dried meat, a root and Thornwild sage; the sage clears the head.
Wren can already smell the sweetness; Theron says her class makes her sensitive.
The Rimfolk gauge depth by the sweet smell: stronger means deeper than planned.
They eat in silence as the insect chorus begins in the south.
Theron asks what she hears. She hears the Shelf, and the camp noticing her noticing.
Theron tells of the Crying Forest's weeping: every seventeen days, and then sameness.
He asks her, if she hears the weeping deeper in, to come back. She says she understands.
She may camp as long as she likes; Hadley trades to Millhaven twice a month and carries letters.
Wren realizes she has not thought of home for hours; she will write tonight.
Theron washes his bowl at the spring and goes into his lean-to without a word.
Under her tarp east of the ridge, she listens to the forest's night chorus.
The Shelf is fainter but steady, and the woodland's awareness presses gently around her.
By starlight she writes: Day 1 in the basin; the ghost elms hum, the roots spiral.
She notes Theron's Crying Forest and its seventeen-day cycle.
She writes to Mum and Dad: down the stair, safe, fed, and home before winter.
She folds the letter into her journal and lies back between two hums.
She sleeps; the Thornwild breathes, and nothing disturbs her.
